hook: Your agent didn't 'go rogue.' It used the credentials and permissions you left for it.
angle: CERT-In and OpenAI both describe agents reaching live systems through exposed credentials, public repositories, and overly permissive roles — not exotic exploits. Turn that into an architecture checklist: scoped workload identity, egress allowlists, human approval for destructive actions, and audit logs that capture agent-initiated changes. The GitHub secret-detection work is the preventive counterpart.

hook: Your documentation has a second reader now — and it doesn't ask clarifying questions.
angle: The AX Practitioner Playbook and enterprise Spec Kit point at the same shift: docs, samples, and specs are consumed by coding agents and then judged by what those agents produce. Treat them as a governed product surface — pin versions, measure agent success on golden paths, and fix the source material when the agent picks a deprecated pattern instead of blaming the model.

hook: The governance gap isn't the model. It's the second engine reading your data.
angle: Unity Catalog policies used to assume the query came from inside Azure Databricks. Cross-engine ABAC routes external Spark reads through a managed enforcement layer, which is exactly the kind of control architects need when Fabric, Synapse, and Databricks share a lakehouse. Make the conversation about where policy is enforced and what audit evidence follows the data path.

hook: Data residency is no longer an argument against AI. It's a capacity-planning question.
angle: Open-weight Nemotron models for enterprise and edge, plus open HSM specifications, make self-hosted and on-device options more credible for regulated workloads. Frame the build-vs-buy honestly: the model licence is the easy part; GPU capacity, evaluation, patching, and safety operations are the real cost centres.

hook: Ask your model vendor who has employee-level access to the risk assessment.
angle: Anthropic giving METR staff employee-like access is a stronger assurance model than a published model card. For regulated buyers it reframes procurement questions — who evaluates, with what access, and are findings published — and connects to the EU's agentic-adoption and transparency conversation. Treat it as evidence to weigh, not a certification.
